title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a table of contents, or plan, for 'Connexion canonique de Gauss-Manin, Partie 2'. The previous page is that title. It lists what remains to be written after constructing the Gauss–Manin connection.

(0) Top line, partly struck and hard to read. It shows a map from the hypercohomology of the relative de Rham complex, H^0(R f_*(Ω^•_{X/S})) or a Hodge-graded version of it, to H^0 of relative 1-forms Ω^1. Plausible readings:
- the edge map of the Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence, H^1_dR → H^0(Ω^1) or its dual Hodge piece;
- a note on the low-degree part of the Gauss–Manin construction.

(1) Item renumbered '8', formerly '1)': 'Compatibilités pour S, T, E variables'. Here S is the base of f: X → S, and T is presumably the ground scheme relative to which the connection is taken (connection on S/T). E is presumably the coefficient module with integrable connection on X relative to T, so the Gauss–Manin connection lives on R f_*(Ω^•_{X/S} ⊗ E). The task is functoriality of the Gauss–Manin connection under base change and change of coefficients, and transitivity in towers X → S → T.

(2) 'Cas des complexes de De Rham tronqués(?), filtrés, à 2 suites exactes de Hodge–De Rham et transversalité de Griffiths et de Deligne.' The idea is to treat the de Rham complex with its Hodge, i.e. stupid-truncation, filtration σ^{≥p}. The Katz–Oda/Koszul filtration then shows that ∇ maps F^p into F^{p-1} ⊗ Ω^1_{S/T}; this is Griffiths transversality. The goal is to relate the connection to the exact sequences coming from the Hodge filtration. 'Transversalité de Deligne' probably points to Deligne's algebraic treatment, or to the logarithmic (regular singular) setting.

(3) Two variants. In characteristic 0, a 'stratified' variant: Gauss–Manin as a stratification, using the equality of stratified (infinitesimal) cohomology with de Rham cohomology. In arbitrary characteristic, a 'crystalline' variant: Gauss–Manin as the crystal structure on R f_{crys*}.

The next page develops a related construction. It uses stratified-module theory to factor differential operators through Z^1 C_{S/R}, applied to a map Γ(G) → Z^1 (logarithmic derivative g^{-1}dg). The margin asks 'spécial à car. 0 ?'.
errors: No mathematical errors; the page is a plan with no claims to check. The top formula is incomplete and partly struck, so it cannot be verified.

ideas.what: Functoriality and compatibility of the Gauss–Manin connection under variation of base S, ground T and coefficients E
ideas.modern_name: Base change / transitivity properties of the Gauss–Manin connection
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's 'Crystals and de Rham cohomology' (Dix exposés, 1968) sketches the crystalline viewpoint; no full published treatment by him that I know of

ideas.what: Interaction of the Gauss–Manin connection with the Hodge filtration via truncated de Rham complexes
ideas.modern_name: Griffiths transversality (algebraic proof via Katz–Oda filtration)

ideas.what: Stratified (infinitesimal) version in characteristic 0 and crystalline version in arbitrary characteristic of Gauss–Manin
ideas.modern_name: Gauss–Manin as stratification / as crystal structure on higher direct images (R f_crys*)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1966–68, Crystals and de Rham cohomology), Berthelot (1974), Berthelot–Ogus
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes, in Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas (1968)

deep.surprise_reason: This is an outline of standard topics: functoriality, Griffiths transversality, and the stratified and crystalline variants. All were developed in the literature by Katz–Oda, Deligne, Berthelot and Grothendieck himself. It only documents his intended plan for the Gauss–Manin text.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'transgressés' is more plausibly 'tronqués' (truncated de Rham complexes for the Hodge filtration), though the handwriting is uncertain.
Item numbering: the '8' in the margin replaces a struck '1)'; the item reads 'Compatibilités pour S,T,E variables' (underlined), followed by a struck word.
'(cohomologie stratifiée — tire de De Rham)' probably reads '(cohomologie stratifiée = coh. de De Rham)' or similar; 'tire' is doubtful.
'Variantes cristallines en car. quelconque' is correct.
The top line likely begins with a struck or abbreviated symbol (possibly 'Hdg' or 'H^0'), not a clean H^0; the target is H^0(Ω^1_{X/...}).
